note: Minimal inputs kept for replay, not a coverage claim. Coverage comes from the seeded corpora in the fuzz gates; this file is what a reduced failure becomes once it has been found, so the exact bytes are re-run for good rather than depending on a seed still reaching them. `text` is used verbatim; `base64` is base64url for bytes that are not valid UTF-8. Every case must say what it catches.

sections.api_bodies: Request bodies driven at signed API routes and at the typed body deserialisers.
sections.sse_frames: Upstream frame bytes fed to the proxy's usage scanner and to the app's SSE parser.
sections.helper_frames: Whole privileged-protocol frames, length header included.
sections.proxy_bodies: Client chat bodies driven at the inference proxy boundary.

api_bodies.why: Empty body. Serde reports EOF rather than a syntax error, which is a different code path.
Duplicate keys are legal JSON text; last-wins must not become first-wins silently.
A lone high surrogate has no UTF-8 encoding; the decoder must refuse rather than emit a replacement into a stored field.
Nesting past serde_json's recursion limit. A parser without one dies here rather than returning an error.
An unknown field must be refused, not ignored: deny_unknown_fields is what stops a caller smuggling engine configuration through a load request.
A number that overflows f64. Parsing must fail or saturate, never panic.
Invalid UTF-8 inside otherwise well-formed JSON syntax (a bare continuation byte).

sse_frames.why: A data line with no terminating newline at end of stream: EOF must not emit a half-parsed frame or lose a complete one.
CRLF line endings. \r\n is one grapheme cluster in Swift, which hides the LF from a character-level parser.
A field with no colon at all, then a real event: the malformed line must not consume the one after it.
The terminator vLLM sends after the last chunk; it carries no usage and must not reset what was counted.
A data line that is valid JSON but not an object; from_json must return None rather than index into it.

helper_frames.why: Header alone, declaring more payload than follows: the parser must not read past the buffer.
A declared length above MAX_REQUEST_BYTES must be refused on the header, before any payload is buffered.
Zero-length payload: a legal header with nothing to parse.
An operation tag that does not exist. The helper answers a bounded protocol error and runs nothing.
A shell-shaped request, which the typed protocol has no representation for and must never gain one.

proxy_bodies.why: An upstream base URL offered as a chat parameter; it must be dropped, not forwarded.
A bearer credential offered as a chat parameter.
trust_remote_code is arbitrary code execution in the engine's loader; it must never cross the boundary.
A banned generation-control parameter is refused outright rather than dropped, so a caller learns it is not merely ignored.
A model name that is not the loaded one: the proxy must not silently rewrite it into the active engine.
Valid JSON that is not an object; the boundary must reject it rather than treating a missing model as a match.
A JSON null body: `null.get("model")` is None, which must not read as the served name.
